summary: For every finite simple graph G with at least one edge, every complete colouring (proper or not) uses at most 2R'(G) colours, where R'(G) is the sum over edges uv of 1/max(d(u), d(v)). Hence the achromatic number, the pseudoachromatic number and the Grundy number are all at most 2R'(G), which proves Wu-Elphick Conjecture 4.1 (and 4.2) for all graphs with an edge. The literal statement "for any graph" fails exactly at nonempty edgeless graphs, where the achromatic number is 1 and R' is 0; Lean proves this exact truth set. The source excludes isolated vertices in its neighbouring results, so the result is a proof of the intended conjecture.

title: The achromatic number bound by the harmonic index
source: Baoyindureng Wu and Clive Elphick, “Upper bounds for the achromatic and coloring numbers of a graph”, arXiv:1511.00537 (2015). (https://arxiv.org/abs/1511.00537)
statement:
Let $G$ be a graph. The **achromatic number** $psi(G)$ is the largest number of colors in a complete proper vertex coloring, and $R'(G)$ denotes the inverse degree-based index used in the source. **The achromatic-number conjecture.**

$$
\psi(G)\leq 2R'(G).
$$

The source presents this as a conjecture motivated by the preceding bounds. Its status is not resolved in the supplied text.
